scope: Supplemental background-path review of an existing32-point native precision screen. Preserve the original screen and every full-spectrum evaluation; do not rerun spectra or change thresholds.
reason: The frozen precision worker reconstructs nominal CAMB backgrounds without the temporary nonlinear-lensing WantTransfer switch. The separately validated expansion-history adapter already establishes that this can exceed the unchanged rdrag closure threshold.
prerequisite: Fresh parent qualification, original sealed plan, all32complete sealed records, original source/input identities and record/log/spectrum manifests. No incomplete or exception record can be repaired by this review.
procedure: For each unchanged point, reconstruct nominal and doubled-accuracy backgrounds using its finalized theory arguments, physical parameters and native_thermal_parameters. Recompute all original nominal-background closure tests, and verify doubled-background H and rdrag against the original full-spectrum evaluation. Recalculate original likelihood/prior accounting using unchanged saved likelihood values. Only obsolete background-closure flags may be replaced; other failures remain.
physical_and_numerical_invariance: No change to cosmological coordinates, observational likelihoods, priors, full native spectra, likelihood precision controls, point selection, density thresholds or finite-screen spread thresholds. Only the auxiliary background initialization path changes.
validation: All four pinned earlier full-native controls must retain the original plain-background failure where present and pass the unchanged rdrag threshold with the existing thermal adapter; synthetic mutation checks must preserve density failures and reject incomplete records. No new CMB spectra are permitted.
interpretation: The supplemental screen is still a32-point numerical diagnostic, never a posterior qualification or asymptotic convergence proof. Any remaining numerical variation requires its own follow-up. The failed original screen remains part of the provenance.
